title: Is a 40% Bill Negotiation Fee Worth It? The Math
description: Bill negotiation services keep 40% to 50% of what they save, or charge a monthly membership. See what you keep at each saving level, and the free options.
h1: Is a 40% bill negotiation fee worth it?
lead: What you keep after the fee at four saving levels, and how the free options compare.
short_answer: A 40% fee on a $20 monthly discount costs $96 of the $240 you save in a year, so you keep $144. It is worth it only if you would never make the call yourself. Calling your provider or switching to another provider keeps the whole saving, because neither takes a fee from it, though a new provider may charge for installation.

sections.body_html: Our arithmetic. 40% is Billshark's published fee and 50% is BillCutterz's. The $15 membership is Rocket Money Premium+ kept for a full year, before tax. A membership kept for fewer months costs less, and it can cover more than one bill.

sections.h2: Three things that change the answer
sections.body_html:
• How the saving is counted. BestMoney reports that Billshark counts savings over up to 24 months. A fee on two years of savings is twice the figures above. Ask when it is billed.
  • How long the discount lasts. A negotiated price is often a promotion. If it ends early or the provider raises rates, the saving you paid a fee on shrinks.
  • How many bills you have. A flat membership costs the same whether it lowers one bill or four.

sections.h2: When paying the fee is reasonable
sections.body_html: If you know you will never sit on hold with a retention team, keeping 60% of a saving beats keeping none of it. Pay-on-success services also charge nothing when they fail, so the risk is the size of the fee, not a loss.

sections.h2: The two options with no fee
sections.body_html:
Call your provider. One call to the retention team is the same thing a negotiator does. Use our free scripts for Xfinity, Spectrum, AT&T and Cox.

Switch providers. If another provider serves your address, its new-customer price may beat any retention offer. Check your bill free to see what is offered at your ZIP code. We take no share of what you save. If you order through us, the provider may pay us a commission. To see how your bill compares first, read the average internet bill.

faq: How much do bill negotiation services charge?

Billshark charges 40% of the savings and BillCutterz 50%, with no fee if nothing is saved. Rocket Money includes negotiation in its $15-a-month Premium+ plan, and Experian BillFixer is included in eligible paid Experian memberships.
Is the negotiation fee charged up front?
Some services bill the fee after a successful negotiation, on the savings they expect. BillCutterz also lets you pay monthly. Ask how and when the fee is billed before you sign up.
What is the cheapest way to lower an internet bill?
Call your provider's retention team yourself, or switch to another provider at your address. Neither involves a fee on your savings.
